title: Ph.D. Project: A Novel Compilation-Based Approach for Generating Sparse Tensor Accelerators
problem: Sparse tensor irregularity challenges GPU/NPU acceleration, and current point-wise manual FPGA design methodologies do not scale efficiently across diverse sparse scenarios.
motivation: Sparse tensor computing is widely used in deep learning and scientific computing, making efficient hardware acceleration critical for performance.
method: The approach uses a compiler—a tool that translates descriptions into hardware designs—with three components. First, a simple language based on scheduling primitives (basic building blocks for describing how to organize computations) lets you specify what the accelerator should do. Second, a two-step mapping process translates how data flows through computations into actual hardware using sparse meta-operations (reusable patterns for efficient sparse operations). Third, an automated search strategy guided by your actual workload explores different hardware designs and picks the fastest.
key_novelty: The key idea is automatically generating sparse tensor hardware accelerators using a compiler that translates from a simple scheduling-based description language (combining basic building blocks) to hardware using reusable sparse computation patterns.
contributions: Schedule-primitive-based DSL for sparse accelerator design specification
Two-stage sparse meta-operations mapping enabling flexible dataflow-to-hardware translation
Heuristic design space exploration strategy guided by workload characteristics
Automatic FPGA sparse accelerator generation reducing manual design effort
primary_theme: Compiler-driven automatic generation of sparse tensor accelerators on FPGA
